A1.justification: Despite different titles, both PDFs describe WePe and retain matching equations, experiments and results. Both documents, including their complete appendices, provide readable text, equations, figures and tables supporting comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original WePe detection results on ImageNet, LSUN-BEDROOM and GenImage, together with ablations, robustness tests and feature analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds results for trained WePe*, DRCT-2M, additional comparisons, attacks and cartoon failure cases.

M1.justification: The original detector and its feature-similarity score remain. However, v2 introduces WePe*: a supervised calibration objective that separates natural/generated image uncertainty through DINOv2 fine-tuning (Section 3.4, Equation 16), implemented using LoRA in Appendix Q. This substantially extends the previously training-free method.

E1.justification: v2 adds DRCT-2M, with COCO natural images and 16 generator variants covering newer diffusion, Turbo, LCM, ControlNet and reconstruction scenarios (Appendix P, Table 11). It also evaluates nongenerated cartoons and frequency-domain attacks, extending v1's three benchmarks and spatial corruption scenarios.

E2.justification: ImageNet Table 1 adds PatchCraft, FatFormer and DRCT. GenImage adds these methods plus NPR, GenDet and AEROBLADE, while removing LaRE. The Gradient Cuff comparison disappears, and v2 Table 8 evaluates MSP and entropy scoring on classification models. Ojha and UnivFD are matched as the same comparator.

E3.justification: New WePe* experiments introduce training on ProGAN for ImageNet/LSUN, SDv1.4 for GenImage and SDv2 for DRCT-2M, with JPEG/blur augmentation (Appendix Q). GenImage's reported evaluation expands from seven columns excluding SDv1.4 to eight including it. Original WePe's backbone, perturbed blocks and noise ratio remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 expands attack comparisons to frequency-domain perturbations and more detectors, adds classification-score diagnostics and visualizes cartoon failures. It removes v1's Gradient Cuff, CLIP projection and detailed noisy-natural-image ensemble analyses. Existing FID, layer-selection, noise-strength and multiple-perturbation analyses remain; the new FID plot redisplays existing evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over five random seeds and retain the same multiple-perturbation error-bar plot, renumbered from Figure 8 to Figure 10. No changed run count, confidence-interval practice or significance-testing procedure is reported.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results, including WePe* at 95.57 AUROC/94.33 AP on ImageNet and DRCT-2M accuracies of 70.92% for WePe and 91.45% for WePe*. Original WePe ImageNet/LSUN results remain unchanged. GenImage's WePe average changes from 81.27 to 80.84 because SDv1.4 is included. The CLIP result 84.82/84.20 in v2 Table 3 already appeared in v1 Table 11.

T1.justification: v1 provides an uncertainty bound but explicitly leaves broader theoretical justification to future work. v2 retains that bound and adds Bayesian variance derivations, a formal Jacobian-based sensitivity definition, Theorem 3.2 with an Appendix C proof, and an upper-bound gap analysis in Appendix D.

C1.justification: The central uncertainty-based detection claim remains. v2 specifies epistemic uncertainty and invokes theoretical support in the introduction. Performance claims are qualified in Section 4.2: v1 emphasizes training-free WePe's superiority over trained methods, whereas v2 distinguishes good untrained performance from superior average results obtained with trained WePe*.

C2.justification: v2 adds Bayesian and sensitivity-based mechanism explanations and argues why fixed-category OOD scoring is unsuitable. Its limitations emphasize a shrinking uncertainty gap as generators improve and possible calibration through WePe*. The earlier hard-sample caveat gains a concrete cartoon interpretation, while the contamination/machine-unlearning discussion and explicit lack-of-theory limitation disappear.

D1.justification: Appendix Q adds LoRA placement, rank/alpha, AdamW hyperparameters, training-data choices, augmentation and an ACC threshold-selection description. v2 also supplies a code repository address and DRCT-2M access information. Conversely, v1's detailed resizing, cropping, format-matching and padding instructions are removed; this establishes lost documentation, not changed preprocessing.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands Bayesian, uncertainty and OOD positioning, including Neal, McAllester, Van der Vaart, DEUP and Ferrante, alongside newer detector discussions. The dedicated review of random-weight-perturbation regularization and adversarial work disappears, as do the Gradient Cuff and machine-unlearning connections.

P1.justification: The title and abstract are rewritten, and the introduction and method narrative are substantially reorganized around epistemic uncertainty. v2 adds Preliminaries, moves Related Work from Section 2 to Section 5, reorganizes the appendices, relocates limitations and adds a conference checklist.

P2.justification: v2 redraws similarity and perturbation plots, adds a cartoon figure and plots previously tabulated FID evidence. It expands comparison tables, adds attack/OOD/DRCT-2M tables and moves GenImage and LSUN results into the appendices. Table grouping, highlighting, figure proportions and surrounding layout change substantially.

improvement.justification: Broader comparisons, WePe*, concrete failure cases and training details strengthen the empirical account. However, the claimed theoretical advance contains an unestablished step from task-loss optimization to near-zero feature sensitivity (Appendix C, Equation 27), replacing v1's explicit acknowledgment that justification was missing. Detailed preprocessing and noise-ensemble evidence are also removed. These substantial benefits and rigor/reproducibility losses leave the net quality direction unclear.
